call_points.text: Spinning is sold forward about 90-95 days in exports and 45-50 days domestic; April-May price gains should show in Q2.
US fabric orders were lost to a missed sampling season; business has improved in the last month and better volumes are expected in 2-3 months.
Dhar PM MITRA land expected by December, but construction waits for power, which management does not expect before June 2027.
Asked for cotton inventory levels, management declined to share them.
Asked to quantify the margin moderation, management said it could not give numbers, citing uncertainty over inventory and yarn prices.
About 12-13 million spindles closed permanently in India over three years, with little new capacity announced, supporting spinning economics.
Management expects Q1FY27 to be better than last year on current yarn, cotton and rupee levels.
Most Indian spinners are sold forward for two to three months on exports.
About 90% of the spinning modernization is done; the rest should finish in the next 6-8 months.
Green power projects, including biomass boilers, are expected to be commissioned in the next 1-2 months.
New land in PM MITRA Park, Madhya Pradesh, is expected by December or January; plans to be finalised in two to three months.
The performance fabrics plant and the fourth cotton fabric line are commissioned but not fully utilised; 6-9 months to ramp.
Cotton inventory cover is normally 6-8 months at year-end; new cotton arrivals start in October.
Management declined to give its own cotton purchase cost, citing market CCI prices instead.
Spread sustainability depends on New York futures, Chinese demand and the war, which management says it cannot predict.

operating_notes.text: Yarn spreads widened to $0.90-0.95 from $0.60-0.65 four months earlier, a 40-50% improvement, with FY26 industry average spread no more than $0.65.
China is buying about 30 million kg of Indian yarn a month versus 7-8 million kg historically, lifting Indian yarn exports to about 120 million kg a month.
Direct exports have held at 44-45% of revenue, and cotton inventory cover is normally 6-8 months at year-end.
Q1FY27 cotton-yarn spread was about USD0.90 per kg against a historical USD0.85-1.00 and USD0.60-0.70 in the last 2-3 years.
Spinning order book is about 90-95 days in exports and 45-50 days domestic; one-third of yarn goes to exports, one-third domestic and one-third captive.
China and Bangladesh take about 60% of India's yarn exports; India's monthly yarn exports rose to about 110 million kg from under 100 million kg.
